findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wallet_transfer, oracle_register, contribute_relations · Private data: look_from, relationships, nearby, map_viewport, company, joules_balance, verify_proof, transparency_latest, balance_proof, bridge_proof, market_provide, market_request, wallet_transfer, joules_deficit, oracle_register, oracle_assignments, oracle_deregister · Public sink: verify_proof, balance_proof, bridge_proof, market_provide, market_request, market_accept, wallet_transfer, oracle_register, oracle_assess, oracle_deregister, contribute_relations, contribute_stats, contribute_submissions, contribute_receipts · Destructive: oracle_register.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wallet_transfer, oracle_register, contribute_relations · Private data: look_from, relationships, nearby, map_viewport, company, joules_balance, verify_proof, transparency_latest, balance_proof, bridge_proof, market_provide, market_request, wallet_transfer, joules_deficit, oracle_register, oracle_assignments, oracle_deregister · Public sink: verify_proof, balance_proof, bridge_proof, market_provide, market_request, market_accept, wallet_transfer, oracle_register, oracle_assess, oracle_deregister, contribute_relations, contribute_stats, contribute_submissions, contribute_receipts · Destructive: oracle_register

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
